images.title: Every diameter folds a circle
images.purpose: Show that a circle folds onto itself along any diameter by drawing three different diameters of one circle.
images.composition: One large circle centred with generous white space around it.
images.exact_structure: One large teal #0072B2 outline circle with a centre dot. Through the dot, 3 diameters, 60 degrees apart: one vertical in reddish purple #CC79A7 and two slanted in amber #E69F00. They split the circle into 6 equal sectors. Exactly 1 circle, 3 diameters, 1 dot.
labels: Every diameter is a mirror line
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a line that does not pass through the centre
images.takeaway: A circle folds onto itself along every line through its centre.
images.description: A teal circle with three diameters through its centre, one vertical and two slanted, 60 degrees apart.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to imagine folding along each drawn diameter and say that the halves match.

image_decisions.why: Folding a circle along many diameters is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
